title.narrative: Modernization and restructuring of the road sector

description.narrative: The development objective of the Modernization and Restructuring of the Roads Sector Project for Croatia is to strengthen the institutional effectiveness, enhance the operational efficiency, and increase the debt service capacity of Croatia's road sector. The project comprises of three components. The first component, institutional strengthening and sector reforms objective to establish an institutional framework for the road sector, including through: financial transaction advisor; transport sector planning and road sector governance and monitoring; and implementation support. The second component, operational restructuring of road sector companies objective is to implement management tools and carry out the revenue enhancement and cost rationalization actions required to improve operational and financial sustainability of the road sector companies, including through: road classification and standards; road asset management system; rationalization of operations and business functions - motorways; tolling; operational and business rationalization of hrvatske ceste (HC); and road safety. The third component, debt optimization - up to EUR 4 billion of the road sector statement of expenditures (SOEs) EUR 5.2 billion of debt may be optimized. International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD's) direct involvement relates to a first refinancing mobilized by the government with the support of an investment project financing (IPF) guarantee objective is to mobilize commercial financing for the road sector SOEs to refinance their short term and expensive loans (guaranteed refinancing facility).
The objective of the Project is to strengthen the institutional effectiveness, enhance the operational efficiency and increase the debt service capacity of Croatia's road sector.

comment.narrative: <p>Target was achieved, and information was confirmed by HC.</p>

title.narrative: Gender balancing - Ratio of women in the motorway sector after retrenchment

comment.narrative: <p>HAC did not meet the target since the new e-tolling system has not been implemented. The fully automated tolling system was expected to be accompanied by retrenchment of predominantly male employees engaged in tolling (and maintenance), expected to shift the staffing gender ratio through new posts in administrative services.</p>

title.narrative: Citizen engagement - Maintain full responsiveness rate to comments and grievances from citizens

comment.narrative: <p>Target was achieved. Overall as regards citizen engagement, the communication consultancy has been completed and has contributedto the Ministry's and SOEs' capacities in improving communication and citizen engagement more generally. The websites of the Ministry (www. mmpi.gov.hr), HAC (www.hac.hr) and HC (www.hrvatske-ceste.hr) include clear contact links and details for citizen/user communication.  </p>

title.narrative: Weighted average maturity of road sector companies' debt

comment.narrative: <p>Target was not met.</p>

title.narrative: Status of implementation of new financing strategy for HAC, ARZ and HC as implemented under the coordination of the National Government [A.1]

comment.narrative: <p>The target was achieved and refinancing and rescheduling were successfully completed without the Bank’s guarantee. Withoutthe transaction services provided under the project, the sector would probably have collapsed due to the huge impending debt repayments.</p>

actual.value: Financing strategy approved; execution of debt optimization transactions at three stages through 2019

title.narrative: Status of implementation of new tolling revenue enhancement measures [B.4]

comment.narrative: <p>This target was not met; however, the TA findings financed under the loan served as a basis for applying for funding under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan, which has been granted. Bidding documents are under preparation, and the tender is expected to be launched in July 2022. A new e-tolling system is planned to be implemented in 2025.</p>

actual.value: New tolling strategy approved by the MSTI and advanced preliminary design completed

title.narrative: Percent Reduction in Operating Cost of Motorways relative to baseline: HAC and ARZ [B.3]

comment.narrative:
<p>Target was not met mainly because the new tolling system, which was assessed to bring significant reduction in operating costs, was not implemented.  </p>
<p>The baseline value was formally revised in 2018 as per companies financial and audit reports.</p>

<p>DSCR was not met (if the indicator is less than 1x the companies are unable to cover its debt out of its cash flows). DSCR was on track for HC and HAC in October 2020 (per ISRs, it was 1.15 for HAC and 1.34 for HC) reflecting progress made as a result of debt optimization and initial effectiveness and efficiency mesures; albeit the positive trend was reversed due to revenue losses caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. However, the introduction of new economic and fiscal policy guidelines for 2020-2022, includes specific targets for State-Owned Enterprise to achieve surpluses, and importantly, introduce the obligation to use these surpluses to prioritizedebt repayment before any investment expenditures. This means that debt repayment is hard-wired into the policy. Althouth the targets were not achieved, the debt re-profiling that took place in several stages and which resulted from the financial modelling conducted under project-financed TA, has considerably smoothened the debt profile of the companies.</p>
<p>Baseline values were formally revised for all the companies in 2018 (amended Supplemental Letter 2) as per the companies’ financial and audit reports.</p>

title.narrative: Operating Expense Ratio (Total Operating Expenses / Total Operating Revenue)

comment.narrative:
<p>Targets were not achieved. During the implementation, it became clear that even though reforms were being made, HC would have been unable to achieve the target in the absence of full control over critical parameters - such as the revenues received from fuel levies or occasional demands to integrate more county roads into its network. These decisions were under the government’s purview while impacting both operating revenue and operational and maintenance expenses. Target was no longer meaningful for HC, when it was realized that the length of HC network was increased by more than 5% through reclassification, partly including expressways. This was recorded in Aide memoirs and Bank’s communication urging the government to restructure the project.</p>
<p>To note is tht the baseline value for HC was revised (compared to original value set in PAD) in 2018 (through amended Supplemental Letter 2) per findings of the company’s financial and audit reports.</p>

<p>HAC target was exceeded, with its LLCR ratio indicating improved solvency and an improvement in its ability to service its debt over the long term, while HC’s target was not met. As indicated under section on factors affecting the implementation, HC faces ad-hoc transfers of roads into its network, which aggrevates its financial management and performance. In addition to that, HC target was not achievable due to disruption caused by cash flow related to the largest infrastructure project - Peljesac bridge funding (co-financing is mandatory for all EU-funded projects) as well as increased transfers to County Road Agencies (ZUCs). This similarl affected DSCR and Debt to CFADS.</p>
<p>Baseline values were formally revised for all the companies in 2018 (amended Supplemental Letter 2) as per the companies’ financial and audit reports. </p>

title.narrative: Weighted Average toll revenue per Vehicle-Km travelled [B.4]

comment.narrative: <p>The indicator is falling short of the target by a small margin. The baseline value was formally revised in 2018 for ARZ as per the company’s financial and audit reports.</p>

title.narrative: Operating Expenditures per kilometer of road network

comment.narrative:
<p>Targets were not met.</p>
<p>To note is that the baseline values for HAC and ARZ were formally revised in 2018 (amended Supplemental Letter 2) as per the companies’ financial and audit reports.</p>

title.narrative: Staff per Kilometer of road under operation (motorways) [B.3]

comment.narrative: <p>Target was not met due to the delay in the implementation of a new e-tolling system. The baseline value for ARZ was formally revised in 2018 as per the company’s financial and audit reports.</p>

<p>This indicator was not achieved. Similar to the comment under the DSCR indicator, the debt to CFADS ratio indicator was proposedto be replaced by the reference to newly introduced economic and fiscal policy guidelines for 2020-2022. The guidelines included specific targets for State-Owned Enterprise to achieve surpluses, and an obligation to use these surpluses to prioritize debt repayment before any investment expenditures, thus making the original indicator irrelevant.</p>
<p>Baseline values were formally revised for all the companies in 2018 as per the companies’ financial and audit reports. </p>

title.narrative: Reduction in Operating Cost for State Roads relative to baseline: HC [B.6]

comment.narrative: <p>Target was not achieved.</p>

title.narrative: Ability of MSTI to monitor and enforce performance of motorway and road companies using Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and standardized accounting measures

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator is on track to be fully achieved by mid-2022, with service-level agreements due to be signed in Q2 2022. Corporate governance plans were adopted in 2017, and a new institutional set-up of sector companies was completed with merger of companies in 2018. KPIs and accounting standards have been in place and endorsed. Notably, the Government adopted amendments to the Road Act in December 2021, which was a prerequisite for the  standardized accounting measures – applied as of January 2022.</p>

actual.value: Service-level agreements will be signed in Q2 2022, and standardized accounting measures are applied as of January 2022

title.narrative: Operational status of Planning Department established within MSTI [A.2]

baseline.value: Inexistent planning and coordination functions within MSTI

comment.narrative: <p>The target was met.</p>

title.narrative: Ability of MSTI to plan road sector investments

comment.narrative: <p>This target has been achieved to a significant extent, with key segments in implementation – a MSTI planning department strengthened, a transport strategy in place and financial strategy updates. The road asset management system (RAMS), which shouldhave informed the rolling investment plans, has not been finalized per original project plans. However, project TA contributed to HC’s own asset management system being developed, with some segments of the system already applied and informing the HC investment plans. So far, a single database of public roads in Croatia was established as a basis for a new platform for spatial monitoringof all road activities, whereas the Croatian Roads operate under a four-year Program of construction and maintenance of public roads (approved by the Government) and a financial program for any upcoming year with projections for two more years, which is subject to the endorsement of the Parliament.</p>

actual.value: The planning department under MSTI was created in 2017 and renamed to "Road Infrastructure Project Financing and Support Service" since January 2021; the transport strategy approved and in force

title.narrative: Status of implementation of improved and harmonized accounting standards [A.3]

comment.narrative: <p>The target was met.</p>

actual.value: Amendment to Roads Act approved in December 2021, and harmonized accounting standards applied as of January 2022.

title.narrative: Status of Implementation of Road Asset Management System (RAMS) development and incorporation in planning [B.2]

baseline.value: Road sector agencies and companies do not have integrated RAMS

comment.narrative: <p>Target was not met due to unsatisfactory work delivered by the consultant, which delayed the overall RAMS implementation. However, based on a study’s findings HC is developing its own RAMS, expected to be fully operational in a two-year time.</p>

actual.value: RAMS technical specifications and bidding documents are completed, but the procurement was not launched and the system is not implemented. HC is developing its own RAMS based on the study completed under the project.

title.narrative: Status of implementation of end-performance road maintenance standards [B.1]

comment.narrative: <p>Target was partially achieved, as HC will apply new maintenance standards in the next framework agreement (the current one is still in force).</p>

actual.value: Maintenance standards consultancy completed. Standards for HAC and HC were incorporated into new rulebooks and applied from January2021 in HAC, and will be applied in HC from January 2023 with the new four-year framework agreement.

title.narrative: Private Direct Mobilization (Debt Refinancing & Rescheduling with support of IBRD Guarantee)

comment.narrative: <p>The target was exceeded. Debt refinancing and rescheduling carried out between 2017 and 2019 supported through a debt optimization strategy prepared by the financial advisor were extremely successful. Sovereign bond issuance in November 2017 used to refinance EUR 1.275 billion was the most favorable one realized in the international capital markets with the 12-year maturity. Rescheduling was done in April 2018, with the same maturity. Net interest savings for road sector companies are EUR 56 million per year.</p>

actual.value: Refinanced: > 900 mn EUR (all companies) Rescheduled: > 2.9 bn EUR
